subject.title: [Bug]: Agents keep writing literal \n into Python files via unquoted heredocs / bash -c

question: Should OpenClaw treat prevention of shell-escaping mistakes as core agent guidance, or leave syntax enforcement to each user workspace’s existing pre-commit and CI tooling?
rationale: The report proposes both a product-behavior preference and a repository/workspace policy mechanism; source-level evidence is needed before choosing a core enforcement boundary.

options.title: Clarify preferred write path
options.body: Document or strengthen the existing structured file-edit path after confirming it prevents this failure, without adding a Python-specific global checker.

options.title: Add opt-in workspace validation
options.body: Design an explicit, language-aware validation surface only if maintainers want OpenClaw to own pre-commit-style checks.

options.title: Keep enforcement project-local
options.body: Leave syntax checking to repository hooks and CI while retaining only general safe-shell authoring guidance.

recommendation.title: Clarify preferred write path
recommendation.body: Document or strengthen the existing structured file-edit path after confirming it prevents this failure, without adding a Python-specific global checker.

likelyOwner.reason: A concrete owner requires current-main history for the agent tool-selection and instruction surfaces.
